name: codex-mail-bridge
description: Read selected Thunderbird and classic Outlook accounts in Codex, including Office 2019. Requires a signed-in desktop mail account.

interface.longDescription: Requires an existing signed-in Thunderbird or classic Outlook account. Sign in and sync the needed mail in that client before use; keep classic Outlook running in that profile. Read explicitly selected accounts in Codex, including Office 2019 without Microsoft 365. Search by date or this/last week/month in the user's time zone. Search returns bounded metadata by default; request snippets when useful, page through body sections and control a conversation's total body budget. Broader reviews can continue Outlook candidate windows or partition by date/folder. Find attachments by subject/date/sender/filename, list one message, then hand off only needed originals up to 10 MiB. Originals use temporary local paths/resource links for host file tools; image pixels require include_image:true. No PDF/Office parsers, OCR, attachment execution, implicit bulk delivery or cloud upload receipt. No send, draft-save, delete, move, read-state, forced-sync or policy changes. Thunderbird uses registered index/cache paths and bounded mbox/maildir lookup; unavailable/unsafe layouts fail closed. Outlook uses its running classic COM profile, rejects shared stores and protected/linked/OLE/embedded-message attachments. Searches/caches can be partial. Temporary exports expire lazily or on normal exit; crashes/locks can leave files. Node.js/Python required, plus Windows PowerShell 5.1 for Outlook. IANA time zones need local timezone data; fixed offsets such as +09:00 work without extra packages. New capabilities have synthetic tests; live provider/installed-host attachment validation remains pending. New Outlook and Mac/web Outlook unsupported. No Cyp Soft backend or tracking. Retrieved mail/files/images reach the AI host. Independent Cyp Soft project; no affiliation with Mozilla, Microsoft or OpenAI.
defaultPrompt: Help me choose one Thunderbird account and check its local mail index.
Find recent emails about a project in my selected Thunderbird account.
Find a requested attachment by subject and date, then hand off only that original file.
